title: Longest Substring Without Repeating
statement: Write `longest_unique(s)` that returns the length of the longest substring of `s` with all unique characters. `s` contains lowercase letters only.

predict_steps.prompt: Window 'abc' is valid. Next char 'a' repeats. What should left do?
predict_steps.hint: Shrink until the duplicate is gone.

reference_solution:
def longest_unique(s):
    seen = set()
    left = 0
    best = 0
    for right, ch in enumerate(s):
        while ch in seen:
            seen.remove(s[left])
            left += 1
        seen.add(ch)
        best = max(best, right - left + 1)
    return best

learn_quiz.question: When a duplicate appears, which side shrinks?
A set in the window tracks?
Each index enters the window how many times ideally?

viva.question: Why does a variable window find the longest substring without repeats in linear time?
expected_points: the right pointer expands across each character once
the left pointer only moves forward when a duplicate appears
each index advances at most once so work is linear
the window always stores a range of distinct characters

viva.question: What is the answer for an empty string or a string of all unique characters?
expected_points: an empty string has length zero
an all-unique string has length equal to the whole input
the window never shrinks if every character is new
those extremes still obey the distinct-character invariant

viva.question: Why move left past the previous index of a repeated character?
expected_points: that restores uniqueness inside the window
the old occurrence can no longer collide with the new one
the invariant is that every character in the window appears once
leaving the old index inside would keep a duplicate
